title: Establishment of a biosample bank of radon-exposed persons for the comprehensive investigation of biological effects of radiation
summary: A ‘radon biobank’ is to be set up at the Federal Office for Radiation Protection (BfS) to analyse the biological effects of radon on the human body. The data will be used to improve risk modelling after low-dose radiation and will serve as a basis for the further development of radon regulations. A particular focus is on researching possible age- and gender-specific effects in the context of different radon exposures in order to identify particularly sensitive groups of people. The University Medical Centre Göttingen (UMG) is responsible for the collection of biosamples and data collection. Various biomaterials (e.g. blood and saliva) are to be collected from 600 test subjects (adults and minors) from homes with high (>300 Bq/m3) and low (<40 Bq/m3) radon exposure. In addition, detailed information on the health status, lifestyle and other occupational or medical exposures of the test subjects will be collected.
conditions: Analyses of various biological effects in different age and sex groups

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Individuals in households where the radon concentration has been measured for one year and was either above 300 Bq/m3 or below 40 Bq/m3 on average.
Who have lived in this dwelling for at least five years at the time of data collection and biosampling or, in the case of younger persons, their entire life to date.
Exclusion criteria:
Persons who do not wish to participate in the study or who are not capable of giving consent (except children)
Children under 3 years of age
Children who, despite the consent of both parents/guardians, do not agree to participate in the study themselves
Persons with a pronounced language barrier that prevents them from answering the questionnaire adequately
